title: A hymn in Gauri
hookLine: Gauri holds Sukhmani and the Bavan Akhri

lines: PEACE OF MIND HAS A NAME.
cards: Peace of mind has a name in the Guru Granth Sahib, and an address. The name is Sukhmani. The address is a heading on ang two hundred sixty-two: Gauri Sukhmani, Mahala five.
A whole block of year two walked through it. But it's easy to forget the first word of that heading, the one a singer reads before anything else. Before it's Sukhmani, it's Gauri.

teach.h: SUKHMANI DEFINES ITSELF: PEACE, THE NAME.
teach.b: Sukhmani is Guru Arjan's, and it's long: section after section, each opened by a salok. Its first ashtapadi begins with remembering. In paraphrase: remembering, remembering, I find peace.
And its rahao says what the name means: Sukhmani, peace, the nectar of the Lord's Name, which comes to rest in the minds of devotees. The composition defines itself. Now hear it as a Gauri hymn.
A composition that wants to settle a restless mind, slowly, over a long stretch, is at home in that earnest, unhurried sound.
The raga gives Sukhmani its pace before the words give it its meaning.

teach.h: THE BAVAN AKHRI: LETTER BY LETTER.
teach.b: A few pages earlier in Gauri sits a different kind of long hymn, also Guru Arjan's: the Bavan Akhri.

It walks through the alphabet one letter at a time, giving a teaching for each, the way a child learns letters, a word for every sound. Kabir has a Bavan Akhri in Gauri too, further on in the section.
So Gauri holds two of the Granth's patient shapes: peace, built section by section, and wisdom, built letter by letter. Both take time, and Gauri gives them time.
Look back at the week: the order of the ragas, thirty-one moods; Sri Rag and its hymn, which watch now; Majh and its letters of longing; Gauri, earnest and deep, and today, peace in gauri.
Tomorrow the list moves on to Asa.

how: Sukhmani Sahib is recited in Sikh homes and gurdwaras, by individuals or by groups, and is also sung in kirtan in Raag Gauri; the Bavan Akhri is read as part of the Gauri section of the Guru Granth Sahib.

games.q: what does “a hymn in gauri” mean?
o: Sukhmani and the Bavan Akhri, set in Gauri's pace
a hymn sung only at a Sikh funeral
a short verse that opens every raga section

games.q: two hymns in Gauri — tap the pairs.
p: peace, the nectar of the Lord's Name
the earnest pace both are set in

s: Sukhmani stands in its own section, outside any raga
its heading reads Gauri Sukhmani, Mahala five.
Sukhmani's rahao says what its name means
peace, the nectar of the Lord's Name, resting in the minds of devotees.
only Guru Arjan wrote a Bavan Akhri in Gauri
Kabir has one in Gauri too, further on in the section.

games.q: you want to teach a whole way of living, patiently, so a learner can follow it step by step. what shape do you give it?
o: a walk through the alphabet, a teaching for each letter.
games.why: the Bavan Akhri in Gauri walks the letters one at a time, giving a teaching for each, the way a child learns to read.

practice: If you can, let the opening of Sukhmani, sung in Gauri, play through the sit without chasing the meaning.
Otherwise make its first idea a breath, remembering on the way in, peace on the way out, slower than feels natural, and when a thought pulls you away, come back as if starting the next section.
If you pray, let the breath carry Waheguru instead.

wordCard.voice: A hymn in Gauri. Sukhmani, Guru Arjan's long hymn of peace, and the Bavan Akhri, teaching letter by letter, both set in Gauri's earnest pace. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: Sukhmani, Guru Arjan's hymn of peace in Raag Gauri.

carryVoice: Your line: peace in gauri. Peace built section by section, wisdom built letter by letter. That's the week.

sources.ref: Gauri Sukhmani M5, Ang 262 (rahao: sukhmanee sukh amrit prabh naam, bhagat janaa kai man bisraam; first ashtapadi: simrau simar simar sukh paavau)
